text: Families want to know what the numbers mean. Scout drafts a plain-language summary, but a doctor always approves the words.
Remember: a doctor reads, finishes and approves the summary before it goes out.
Juniper's results are final. Open them.
The email button is grey, and Scout says why.
Scout drafts it from the result and Juniper's chart, to Maria by her first name. It's a draft until you approve it.
The next steps are yours to write. Click Edit.
Scout won't let you approve it with the gap still there.
Once the wording is approved, Email lab summary and report appears right beside it. It sends the summary, with IDEXX's report attached.
Check who it's going to, and read it once more before you send.
Email lab report sends just IDEXX's report with a short note. It only needs the result reviewed.
Medical note opens on top of the result. Write your read of it.
Wrap up puts it on Juniper's chart, and you're still on the result.
If IDEXX updates a result after you approved, the summary needs approving again. Draft it again, and approve it.
The most common mistake: approving the draft without reading it. Remember: a doctor reads, finishes and approves the summary before it goes out.
